source.author: Admin (Defence Security Asia)
source.source_class: third-party defence trade press — secondary reporting, not a primary document. It carries no direct quotation from the Ministry of Defence, only a paraphrase.

test_facts_as_reported.outcome: flight validated all operational and technical parameters (paraphrased from MoD)

technical_specifications_as_reported.guidance: ring-laser-gyro inertial navigation, redundant micro-navigation system, digital controls, thrust-vector control

cross_source_agreement.note: Three independent characterisations of the same missile. They agree on physical specification and disagree on class, which is a definitional dispute, not a factual one.

rows.comment: MRBM vs IRBM is a threshold convention (3,000 km by some definitions, 3,500 km by others), not a disagreement about performance.
DSA quotes the top of the CSIS band as a flat figure.

rows.csis: inertial with ring laser gyroscopes; flexseal thrust vectoring
rows.dsa: ring-laser-gyro inertial + redundant micro-nav, digital controls, TVC

cross_source_agreement.reading: DSA's thrust figures (710 kN / 39.5 kN), casing materials and CEP are identical to the CSIS profile, so the two are not independent on the technical side — they share a source lineage. The test facts, by contrast, match the MoD announcement directly and ARE independently corroborating.

editorial_claims_not_test_facts.claim: 'from suitable deployment areas in eastern or northeastern India, Agni-4 could place strategic centres across most mainland China within reach'
editorial_claims_not_test_facts.status: ANALYSIS, not an observation from this test
editorial_claims_not_test_facts.note: A range-circle inference from a stated 4,000 km figure and hypothetical basing. Nothing in the 6 August event, the NAVAREA warnings or the NOTAMs speaks to deployment location or targeting. Recorded as the outlet's framing.

editorial_claims_not_test_facts.claim: test 'validated an operational 4,000-kilometre nuclear-capable ballistic missile'
editorial_claims_not_test_facts.note: The MoD said the launch validated operational and technical parameters. It did not state a range figure, did not say 'operational', and did not mention a nuclear role. Those are the outlet's additions.

editorial_claims_not_test_facts.claim: No First Use policy and nuclear triad context
editorial_claims_not_test_facts.note: Standing Indian declaratory policy; not derived from this test.

corroborates: Strategic Forces Command as the conducting authority
does_not_address: which of the two declared windows was used
why the airspace closure (VED-52, 1430-1730Z) does not match the strategic maritime window (819/26, 1230-1530Z)
relevance_to_this_collection.note: This is the third source to place the launch at Chandipur rather than Abdul Kalam Island. Taken with the VED-52 geometry — which encloses Chandipur and excludes the island by 10.6 km — the weight of evidence is that this launch was NOT from the island this system's AOI is centred on.
